canonical_question: If the MA-SPS-HPT specimen had been annealed to remove oxides before HPT, would the high dislocation density and fine grain size still be achievable without cracking?

question_variants.question: If the MA-SPS-HPT specimen had been annealed to remove oxides before HPT, would the high dislocation density and fine grain size still be achievable without cracking?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided evidence describes the high oxygen content and cracking of the MA-SPS-HPT specimen but does not contain data or mechanisms regarding a hypothetical scenario where oxides were removed via annealing prior to HPT to prevent cracking while maintaining microstructure.

answers.answer: The text confirms that the MA-SPS sample had the highest oxygen concentration and that the specimen broke into several pieces during HPT, with the results deemed disputable. However, there is no evidence discussing a counterfactual annealing step or the feasibility of achieving the same dislocation density and grain size without cracking under such modified conditions.
answers.mechanism: Brittleness associated with high oxygen content
answers.boundary_limitation: No data on annealed samples prior to HPT
evidence_spans: Very high hardness of the MA-SPS-HPT specimen (584 HV10) can be ascribed to the high oxygen content in solid solution and also the presence of oxide particles that caused additional strengthening.
As seen in Figure 8 hardness was correlated with oxygen content in the sample.
It should be pointed out that the MA-SPS-HPT specimen was broken into several pieces during the HPT process and therefore the results of such specimen are disputable.
